title: Genus raising cover with an equivariant stable pointed model
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, and $f:P\to S$ an H-projective flat finitely presented morphism with $P$ integral of finite type over $k$, pure one-dimensional geometric fibres and smooth geometrically integral generic fibre. Let $M\subset P$ be closed with reduced generic fibre finite etale, and let a finite group $H$ act compatibly on $k,P,S,f$, preserving $M$. Put $K_0=k(S)$ and $F_0=k(P)$.

There are normal integral projective finite-type $k$-schemes $S_1,S_2$, finite groups $H_1,H_2$ with surjections $H_2\xrightarrow{\rho_2}H_1\xrightarrow{\rho_1}H$, compatible actions, an equivariant finite surjection $S_1\to S$, an equivariant H-projective alteration $S_2\to S_1$, and an integral finite-type $k$-scheme $Q$ with an equivariant finite surjection $Q\to P\times_S S_1$. Write $K_i=k(S_i)$ and $F_1=k(Q)$. The extensions $K_1/K_0,F_1/F_0,K_2/K_1$ are finite separable. For $A_1=\ker\rho_1$ and $N_2=\ker\rho_2$, the diagram identifies $F_1^{A_1}=F_0$, $K_1^{A_1}=K_0$ and $K_2^{N_2}=K_1$. The family $Q/S_1$ is H-projective with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres; its generic fibre is smooth geometrically integral of genus at least two. Every morphism from $\mathbf P^1_\Omega$ to any geometric fibre $Q_\Omega$ is constant. The reduced generic inverse image of $M$ is a finite set of distinct $K_1$-rational points $p_i$, stable as a set under $H_1$.

There is an H-projective stable pointed curve $(W\to S_2,s_i)$ with an $H_2$-action compatible with that on $S_2$ and preserving the union of sections. It has an $H_2$-equivariant generic pointed identification $(W_\eta,s_i(\eta))\simeq(Q_{\eta_1},p_i)\times_{K_1}K_2$. The markings may be empty. The action on $W$ is uniquely determined by its generic restriction, even when it permutes the markings. Etale means [def-weil-etale-morphism], genus means [def-pc-genus], and $\mathbf P^1$ is the projective line of [def-kun-projective].

Field, integrality, properness, finite type, geometric integrality, dimension, H-projectivity, finite morphisms, surjectivity, function fields and field extensions use [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension] and [def-pc-field-tower]. H-projective means a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target. Normal means all local rings are integrally closed domains. An alteration is a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes, with finite function-field extension and finite over a dense open. Actions may be nonfaithful and semilinear on the ground field; equivariance through a group surjection always includes its action on that field. Purely inseparable means every element has a characteristic-power in the smaller field in positive characteristic, and equality in characteristic zero. Flatness, finite presentation, smoothness, geometric fibres, closed immersions and fibre products use [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-weil-closed-immersion] and [def-pc-fibre-product]. Stable pointed curve means [def-sfb-stable-pointed-curve]; its sections may be permuted. Quasi-split means [def-sfb-quasi-split-nodal-fibres].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-high-genus-equivariant-cover] to $P/S,M,H$. Its hypotheses hold: the given flatness and finite presentation are extra assumptions, while it requires H-projectivity, pure one-dimensional geometric fibres, smooth geometrically integral generic fibre, the finite etale reduced generic marking and compatible finite-group actions. Retain $S_1,Q,H_1$, write $\rho_1:H_1\twoheadrightarrow H$, and put $K_1=k(S_1)$, $F_1=k(Q)$, $A_1=\ker\rho_1$. The cited statement gives the finite surjections, normal projective base, integral total space, H-projectivity and fibre dimensions, both finite separable extensions, $F_1^{A_1}=F_0$, $K_1^{A_1}=K_0$, and the rational distinct generic markings stable under $H_1$. It also gives constancy of every map from a geometric projective line to a geometric fibre. To verify the genus hypothesis over $K_1$ itself, let $C=Q_{\eta_1}$. It is projective by [lem-pc-projective-base-change] applied to $Q/S_1$, and hence proper by [lem-pc-projective-proper]; geometric integrality includes geometric reducedness and connectedness, so [lem-pc-h0-geom-connected] gives $H^0(C,\mathcal O_C)=K_1$. Apply [lem-pc-genus-base-change] to an algebraic closure of $K_1$. The resulting geometric curve is smooth and integral, so is its own normalization; the cover lemma gives its genus at least two. Genus invariance therefore gives $g(C)\geq2$.

source.place: §§3.2--3.8, printed pp.605--609; primary publisher scan read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Enumerate the distinct generic marked points as $p_1,\ldots,p_n$, allowing $n=0$. Apply [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-generic-extension] to the smooth projective geometrically integral curve $Q_{\eta_1}/K_1$ with these points. The base $S_1$ is integral projective finite type over $k$, and its generic curve has genus at least two by Step 1. Obtain an integral alteration $r:T\to S_1$, a finite separable extension $k(T)/K_1$, a stable pointed family $(V/T,t_i)$, and its actual labelled generic identification with $(Q_{\eta_1},p_i)_{k(T)}$. This applies even with no markings. No group action on $T$ or $V$ is needed.

source.place: §§3.2--3.8, printed pp.605--609; primary publisher scan read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: Apply the separable case of [lem-sfb-semilinear-galois-alteration-domination] to $r:T\to S_1$ and the semilinear $H_1$-action from Step 1. Its base is normal integral projective finite type over $k$. It gives a finite group $H_2$, a surjection $\rho_2:H_2\twoheadrightarrow H_1$, a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme $S_2$, an equivariant H-projective alteration $b:S_2\to S_1$, and an $S_1$-morphism $t:S_2\to T$. For $K_2=k(S_2)$ and $N_2=\ker\rho_2$, its separable clause says precisely that $K_2/K_1$ is finite separable and $K_2^{N_2}=K_1$. Pull $(V,t_i)$ back along $t$ and call the result $(W/S_2,s_i)$. The arbitrary-base-change assertion of [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-generic-extension] supplies all stable pointed conditions. Pulling its specified generic identification to $K_2$ gives $\alpha:(W_{\eta_2},s_i(\eta_2))\simeq(Q_{\eta_1},p_i)_{K_2}$: since $r$ is an alteration of integral schemes, its generic fibre is $\operatorname{Spec}k(T)$. The generic point of $S_2$ lies over that of $S_1$, so its map through $t$ lands in this generic fibre and induces $k(T)\hookrightarrow K_2$ over $K_1$. Associativity of the fibre products now gives the displayed identification.

source.place: §§3.2--3.8, printed pp.605--609; primary publisher scan read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The generic curve $(Q_{\eta_1},\{p_i\})_{K_2}$ has a semilinear $H_2$-action: use $\rho_2(h)$ on $Q_{\eta_1}$ and $h$ on $K_2$. They agree on $K_1$ by equivariance of $b$. Transfer this action through $\alpha$. For each $h\in H_2$, it gives an isomorphism of unordered generic pointed fibres of the translate $h^*(W,s_i)$ and $(W,s_i)$ over $S_2$. Both families are stable, also after this base change, by [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-generic-extension]. Apply [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-isom-finite]: $S_2$ is finite type over $k$, normal and integral, so each generic isomorphism extends uniquely over $S_2$. The resulting maps over the base automorphisms give the $H_2$-action. Indeed, the composite for $h,h'$ and the extension for $hh'$ have the same generic restriction, so uniqueness makes them equal; the identity and inverses follow the same way. Thus this is a genuine action, semilinear on $k$ through $\rho_1\rho_2$, preserving the union of the sections, and $\alpha$ is equivariant by construction. Uniqueness in the same Isom statement proves that this action is uniquely determined by its generic restriction; no individual marking is required to be fixed.

source.place: §§3.2--3.8, printed pp.605--609; primary publisher scan read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: The stable family $W/S_2$ obtained by base change in Step 3 is projective in the projective-bundle sense permitted by [lem-sfb-stable-pointed-generic-extension]. Since $S_2$ is projective over $k$, choose its closed immersion into some $\mathbf P^N_k$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-ample-invertible] with $A=k$ and $X=S_2$ to obtain an absolute ample invertible module on $S_2$. Now [lem-trf-projective-bundle-to-h-projective] applies to $W\to S_2$ and gives precisely a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over $S_2$. No equivariant embedding is needed: H-projective has the meaning specified in the statement.

source.place: Tag 087S, lemma-projective-over-quasi-projective-is-H-projective, clause (1); ample module supplied by the cited closed-projective-immersion theorem.

proof.text: Take the two group surjections and all the schemes and maps just constructed. Step 1 supplies every clause about $S_1,Q$, $K_1/K_0$, $F_1/F_0$, $A_1$, the genus, absence of rational curves and generic markings. Step 3 supplies every clause about $S_2$, $K_2/K_1$, $N_2$ and the stable generic identification. Steps 4 and 5 supply the equivariant stable pointed action, its uniqueness and H-projectivity. Their actions on $k$ compose through $H_2\to H_1\to H$, so the diagrams have the prescribed semilinear equivariance. These are exactly the required data.

Step 1: lem-sfb-high-genus-equivariant-cover gives the cover clauses, and genus at least 2 over K_1 follows via 01WF, 01W5, h0-geom-connected (H^0=K_1) and genus-base-change(a) applied to the smooth integral geometric generic fibre.
